plans.name: Free
features: AI interviews with a daily limit

items.a: Yes. The path starts at A1: the alphabet, greetings, introducing yourself. Interview practice by trade works best from about A2.

Type your job into “What is your job?” at the top of the page. Roles with a dedicated question set show sample questions right away. For other roles the AI uses the general question set, adapted to the role you enter.

items.q: How accurate is the AI feedback?
items.a: The AI points out grammar mistakes, wrong words and missing points, with a corrected sentence. Scores help you track progress and do not replace a real exam. If you study with a school, your teacher reviews and confirms grades for written work.
The AI shows which words it could not hear clearly in your answer. This is not yet a detailed sound-by-sound pronunciation analysis.
Recordings are turned into text so they can be scored and reviewed. How long they are kept and how to ask for deletion is described in the Privacy Policy.

items.q: Is a mock exam a certificate?
items.a: No. Mock exams simulate the Goethe and telc format, are not affiliated with either organisation and do not replace a certificate.

items.q: I study at a language school. Can we use it together?
items.a: Yes. The school creates classes and assigns work; you do it in the app and your teacher follows and grades it.
You start for free with a daily AI practice allowance, no credit card needed. Paid plans are shown in the app.

meta.title: About us · myDeutschFlow
meta.description: myDeutschFlow is a project by Đinh Huy Cự, a software developer teaching himself German, building the German interview practice tool he needed himself.

hero.sub: myDeutschFlow is a project by Đinh Huy Cự, a software developer teaching himself German to find work in Germany, and building exactly the tool he needed.
hero.photoAlt: Đinh Huy Cự, founder of myDeutschFlow, in a grey suit

ch1.name: The gap
ch1.title: Plenty of study material. Almost nowhere to practise a job interview for your field.
body: Like many others, I am not learning German to pass a test for fun. I am learning it to live, work and get through interviews in German.

Along the way I noticed that Vietnamese learners of German have plenty of material, but almost nowhere to practise speaking and job interviews for their field safely, with expert feedback, and with an understanding of how German employers hire.

about.quote: Every feature comes from a real need, not a guess.

ch2.name: Building it
ch2.title: So I built the tool I needed.
ch2.body: An AI plays a German employer, asks about your actual job and points out what to fix after every answer. Add a day-by-day A1–B1 path and mock exams in the Goethe and telc format. Every job has an interviewer from that line of work.

timeline.name: Step by step
timeline.title: One person, one step at a time.
timeline.solo: There is no team behind this. From the first line of code until today, I have built myDeutschFlow on my own, over more than 1,600 commits.

ch3.name: Growing
ch3.title: It began with Vietnamese learners. It is for everyone preparing to move to Germany.
ch3.body: That gap is not only a Vietnamese one. Anyone moving to Germany for work or vocational training needs to practise interviews for their field, in German. So myDeutschFlow serves three groups, in every job and every country.
